goals.0: What to say when you don't understand: Ich verstehe das nicht
goals.1: Asking for the meaning and the spelling: Was bedeutet …? Wie schreibt man das?
dialog.3.de.3.n: nicht negates the verb — it goes at the end of the sentence
dialog.5.de.2.n: man = people in general; the verb takes the same form as with er (-t)
dialog.6.de.0.n: Do you remember the letter names? You'll practise them again in Unit 2
grammar.0.title: The most useful phrases in class
grammar.0.note: Learn these eight phrases by heart. You'll use them from the first day.
grammar.0.rows.1.0: I'd like to hear it again
grammar.0.rows.7.2: That is correct. / That is wrong.
grammar.1.intro: verstehen is regular; wissen is irregular — ich and er have the same form (weiß), with no -t.
grammar.1.note: Ich weiß nicht. = I don't know. — „wissen“ means knowing facts; „kennen“ (knowing a person or place) is different, and you'll learn it later.
grammar.2.title: „man“ — someone, people in general
grammar.2.text: „Wie schreibt man das?“ literally: how does one write that? = How is that written? With „man“ the verb takes the er form (schreibt, sagt). It works like English “one / you”. Use it to state a general rule or custom without naming a particular person.
quiz.6.why: ich weiß (wissen is irregular, with no -e at the end).
quiz.7.prompt: Put the words in order to make the question: “How do you spell that?”
